```{r setup, include=FALSE}

```

##Load the package and data

```{r load message = FALSE}
#load package
library(codebook)

#import data
raw <- read.csv("C:\\PSY221A\\Data\\Raw Data\\data_doctored.csv")

```

## Hypothesis 1: Controlling for age, level of education, and political views, being a female (categorical IV) predicts higher intensity of love feelings than the other genders at birth (Male and intersex)

##Hypothesis 2: Controlling for age, level of education, gender/sex at birth, and political views, higher willingness to marry a partner without romantic love (continuous IV) predicts lower relationship satisfaction. 

```{r}
#make data with the variables I need in the two hypotheses

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Relationship_status", "Age", "cot_educ",
               "cot_politics", "Love_how_much_1", "Love_would_you_marry_1",
               "prqc_1", "prqc_2", "prqc_3")]

dim(data)

```

##Check particpants IDs

```{r}
#count NA
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId == "", na.rm = T)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID, ])

#remove the known empty record with no ID
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId), ]

```


##Binary Code sex at birth: 1 = Female, 0 = TheOtherSex Male and Intersex
```{r}
data$Sex_birth <- ifelse(data$Sex_birth %in% c(0, 1, 2),
                         data$Sex_birth, NA)
data$Gender_new <- ifelse(data$Sex_birth == 1, 1, 0)


#Turn binary sex_birth into factors with labels
data$Gender_new <- factor(data$Gender_new,
                          levels = c(0,1),
                          labels = c("Male_Intersex","Female"))

table(data$Gender_new, useNA = "ifany")

```


## Validate the other controlling variables: age, level of education, political beliefs
```{r}
summary(data[, c("Age", "cot_educ", "cot_politics")])

table(data$cot_educ, useNA = "ifany")
table(data$cot_politics, useNA = "ifany")

```

##Check the IV and DV variables in the two hypotheses: intensity of love feelings, willingness to marry a partner without romantic love, relationship satisfaction

```{r}
#Check values for the non-combined variables
summary(data[, c("Love_how_much_1", "Love_would_you_marry_1")])

#Check values for the combined variables
summary(data[, c("prqc_1", "prqc_2", "prqc_3")])

```


##Calculate avg relationship satisfaction
```{r}
#Calculate the mean of all three items, if missing one item or two, use the remaining items to calculate their average relationship satisfaction.
data$satisfaction <- rowMeans(data[, c("prqc_1", "prqc_2", "prqc_3")],
                             na.rm = TRUE)

summary(data$satisfaction)

```

## Get variables for H1 and H2
```{r}
#Variables for H1:
h1Data <- data[, c("ResponseId", "Gender_new", "Love_how_much_1",
                   "Age", "cot_educ", "cot_politics")]

#only include item with no missing value
h1Data <- h1Data[complete.cases(h1Data), ]

#Keep those participants in relationship for H2
relData <- data[data$Relationship_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), ]

h2Data <- relData[, c("ResponseId", "Love_would_you_marry_1",
                      "satisfaction", "Age", "cot_educ",
                      "Gender_new", "cot_politics")]

h2Data <- h2Data[complete.cases(h2Data), ]


```

## Check final tables
```{r}
#Check H1 data
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))
table(h1Data$Gender_new)
range(h1Data$Love_how_much_1) 

#Check H2 data
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
table(h2Data$Gender_new)
range(h2Data$Love_would_you_marry_1) 
range(h2Data$satisfaction)
```

## Add labels and generate codebooks

```{r}
#Add descriptions for H1:
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID",
  "Sex at birth: Female vs. Male/Intersex; coded 1=Female, 0=Male/Intersex before conversion to factor",
  "Love intensity: 0=Very little, 100=Very much",
  "Age in years: 18–90",
  "Education: 1=None, 2=Primary, 3=Secondary, 4=High school/technical college, 5=Bachelor, 6=Master, 7=PhD/MD/JD or equivalent",
  "Political views: 1=Far left, 2=Center left, 3=Center, 4=Center right, 5=Far right"
)

#Add description for H2:
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID",
  "Willingness to marry without romantic love: 0=Definitely would not marry, 100=Definitely would marry",
  "Relationship satisfaction: mean of available prqc_1–3 responses; 1=Not at all, 7=Extremely; at least one valid response required; no reverse coding",
  "Age in years: 18–90",
  "Education: 1=None, 2=Primary, 3=Secondary, 4=High school/technical college, 5=Bachelor, 6=Master, 7=PhD/MD/JD or equivalent",
  "Sex at birth: Female vs. Male/Intersex; coded 1=Female, 0=Male/Intersex before conversion to factor",
  "Political views: 1=Far left, 2=Center left, 3=Center, 4=Center right, 5=Far right"
)

#Generate codebooks for H1 and H2
compact_codebook(h1Data)
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## Save the final tables

```{r}
dir.create("data/processed_data", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)


write.csv(h1Data, "data/processed_data/h1Data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(h2Data, "data/processed_data/h2Data.csv", row.names = FALSE)


h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1Data.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2Data.csv")

dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)
```
